key_insight: The paper introduces a universal diffuse-interface surfactant framework that works across all solubility cases and phase-field methods while remaining conservative, leakage-free, Galilean-invariant, and reduction-consistent.
engineering_relevance: It provides a drop-in modeling layer for predicting surfactant transport and Marangoni effects in multiphase CFD, including insoluble, soluble, and partially soluble systems.
method: General three-scalar non-equilibrium transport model for surfactant in both bulk phases and at the interface
Thermochemical-equilibrium reduction to two one-scalar models for common equilibrium scenarios
Coupling to Navier–Stokes via surface tension forces that include Marangoni stress from interfacial concentration gradients
evidence_signal: The framework is validated with 1D analytical transport tests, 2D advection-diffusion convergence studies, and fully coupled drop-in-shear simulations across insoluble, soluble, and partially-soluble cases.
watch_item: Practical use still requires careful parameterization and numerical coupling to the chosen phase-field method to preserve conservation and interface accuracy.
paper_title: A universal diffuse interface modeling framework for surfactants
